# Target Variable Analysis - Price Distribution
print("\n🎯 TARGET VARIABLE ANALYSIS: PRICE")
print("=" * 40)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(16, 12))
fig.suptitle('Car Price Distribution Analysis', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold')

# 1. Histogram with KDE
axes[0,0].hist(df['price'], bins=30, color='skyblue', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7, density=True)
df['price'].plot(kind='kde', ax=axes[0,0], color='red', secondary_y=True)
axes[0,0].set_title('Price Distribution with KDE', fontweight='bold')
axes[0,0].set_xlabel('Price (£)')
axes[0,0].set_ylabel('Density')
axes[0,0].grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# 2. Box plot
sns.boxplot(y=df['price'], ax=axes[0,1], color='lightcoral')
axes[0,1].set_title('Price Box Plot', fontweight='bold')
axes[0,1].set_ylabel('Price (£)')

# 3. Violin plot
sns.violinplot(y=df['price'], ax=axes[1,0], color='lightgreen')
axes[1,0].set_title('Price Violin Plot', fontweight='bold')
axes[1,0].set_ylabel('Price (£)')

# 4. Q-Q plot (for normality check)
from scipy import stats
stats.probplot(df['price'], dist="norm", plot=axes[1,1])
axes[1,1].set_title('Q-Q Plot for Normality Check', fontweight='bold')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Categorical Features Visualization¶

In [13]:
# Categorical Features Visualization
print("\n📊 CATEGORICAL FEATURES VISUALIZATION")
print("=" * 45)

categorical_cols = df.select_dtypes(include=['object']).columns

if len(categorical_cols) > 0:
    # Determine grid size
    n_cols = len(categorical_cols)
    n_rows = (n_cols + 1) // 2
    
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(n_rows, 2, figsize=(16, 5*n_rows))
    fig.suptitle('Categorical Features Distribution', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold')
    
    if n_rows == 1:
        axes = axes.reshape(1, -1)
    
    for idx, col in enumerate(categorical_cols):
        row = idx // 2
        col_idx = idx % 2
        
        # Get value counts
        value_counts = df[col].value_counts()
        
        # Create subplot
        if n_rows > 1:
            ax = axes[row, col_idx]
        else:
            ax = axes[col_idx]
        
        # Bar plot
        bars = ax.bar(range(len(value_counts)), value_counts.values, 
                     color=plt.cm.Set3(np.linspace(0, 1, len(value_counts))))
        ax.set_title(f'{col} Distribution', fontweight='bold')
        ax.set_xlabel(col)
        ax.set_ylabel('Count')
        
        # Add value labels on bars
        for i, bar in enumerate(bars):
            height = bar.get_height()
            ax.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2., height + 0.1,
                   f'{height:,}', ha='center', va='bottom', fontweight='bold')
        
        # Set x-ticks
        ax.set_xticks(range(len(value_counts)))
        ax.set_xticklabels(value_counts.index, rotation=45, ha='right')
        
        # Add percentage labels
        total = len(df)
        for i, (category, count) in enumerate(value_counts.items()):
            percentage = f'({count/total*100:.1f}%)'
            ax.text(i, count/2, percentage, ha='center', va='center', 
                   fontweight='bold', color='white', fontsize=10)
    
    # Hide empty subplots
    for idx in range(len(categorical_cols), n_rows * 2):
        row = idx // 2
        col_idx = idx % 2
        if n_rows > 1:
            axes[row, col_idx].set_visible(False)
        else:
            axes[col_idx].set_visible(False)
    
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
    
else:
    print("No categorical columns found for visualization.")

📊 CATEGORICAL FEATURES VISUALIZATION
=============================================

Distribution of Numerical Features¶

In [15]:
# Distribution of Numerical Features
print("\n📈 DISTRIBUTION OF NUMERICAL FEATURES")
print("=" * 45)

# Calculate grid size
n_cols = len(numerical_cols)
n_rows = (n_cols + 2) // 3  # 3 columns per row

fig, axes = plt.subplots(n_rows, 3, figsize=(18, 5*n_rows))
fig.suptitle('Distribution of Numerical Features', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold')

# Flatten axes for easy iteration
if n_rows > 1:
    axes = axes.flatten()
else:
    axes = axes.flatten() if isinstance(axes, np.ndarray) else [axes]

for idx, col in enumerate(numerical_cols):
    if idx < len(axes):
        # Histogram with KDE
        sns.histplot(df[col], kde=True, ax=axes[idx], color='lightseagreen', alpha=0.7)
        axes[idx].set_title(f'{col} Distribution', fontweight='bold')
        axes[idx].set_xlabel(col)
        axes[idx].set_ylabel('Frequency')
        axes[idx].grid(True, alpha=0.3)
        
        # Add statistics as text
        mean_val = df[col].mean()
        median_val = df[col].median()
        axes[idx].axvline(mean_val, color='red', linestyle='--', alpha=0.8, label=f'Mean: {mean_val:.2f}')
        axes[idx].axvline(median_val, color='green', linestyle='--', alpha=0.8, label=f'Median: {median_val:.2f}')
        axes[idx].legend()

# Hide empty subplots
for idx in range(len(numerical_cols), len(axes)):
    axes[idx].set_visible(False)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

📈 DISTRIBUTION OF NUMERICAL FEATURES
=============================================

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(16, 12))
    fig.suptitle('Price vs Top Correlated Numerical Features', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold')

        if idx < 4:
            # Scatter plot with regression line
            sns.regplot(x=df[feature], y=df['price'], 
                       ax=axes[idx], 
                       scatter_kws={'alpha':0.6, 'color':'blue'}, 
                       line_kws={'color':'red', 'linewidth':2})
            axes[idx].set_title(f'Price vs {feature}\n(Correlation: {corr:.3f})', fontweight='bold')
            axes[idx].set_xlabel(feature)
            axes[idx].set_ylabel('Price (£)')
            axes[idx].grid(True, alpha=0.3)
    
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
else:
    print("Not enough numerical features for scatter plot matrix.")

duplicates = df_processed.duplicated().sum()

    print("🧹 Removing duplicate records...")
    df_processed = df_processed.drop_duplicates()
    print(f"✅ Removed {duplicates} duplicate records")
    print(f"📊 New shape: {df_processed.shape}")
else:
    print("✅ No duplicate records found!")

# Check for missing values
print("\n📝 MISSING VALUES ANALYSIS:")
print("=" * 25)
missing_data = df_processed.isnull().sum()
missing_percentage = (missing_data / len(df_processed)) * 100

missing_df = pd.DataFrame({
    'Column': df_processed.columns,
    'Missing_Count': missing_data.values,
    'Missing_Percentage': missing_percentage.values
})

display(missing_df.style.set_caption("Missing Values Report") \
       .background_gradient(subset=['Missing_Count'], cmap='Reds') \
       .format({'Missing_Percentage': '{:.2f}%'}))

if missing_data.sum() == 0:
    print("✅ No missing values found!")
else:
    print("⚠️ Missing values detected - will handle them in preprocessing")

# Label Encoding for Categorical Variables
print("\n🔤 LABEL ENCODING FOR CATEGORICAL VARIABLES")
print("=" * 50)

from sklearn.preprocessing import LabelEncoder
import copy

# Create a copy of X for encoding
X_encoded = copy.deepcopy(X)

# Identify categorical column indices
categorical_indices = [X_columns.index(col) for col in categorical_features if col in X_columns]

print(f"🔤 Encoding {len(categorical_indices)} categorical features:")
label_encoders = {}

for idx, col_idx in enumerate(categorical_indices):
    col_name = X_columns[col_idx]
    le = LabelEncoder()
    X_encoded[:, col_idx] = le.fit_transform(X_encoded[:, col_idx])
    label_encoders[col_name] = le
    
    print(f"   {idx+1}. {col_name}:")
    print(f"      • Original unique values: {len(le.classes_)}")
    print(f"      • Encoded values: {le.classes_.tolist()[:5]}{'...' if len(le.classes_) > 5 else ''}")

print("\n✅ Label encoding completed successfully!")

# Display encoded features
print("\n📋 FIRST 5 ROWS AFTER LABEL ENCODING:")
X_encoded_preview = pd.DataFrame(X_encoded, columns=X_columns)
display(X_encoded_preview.head().style.set_caption("Features After Label Encoding") \
       .background_gradient(cmap='plasma'))

One-Hot Encoding for Specific Categorical Features¶

In [27]:
# One-Hot Encoding
print("\n🎯 ONE-HOT ENCODING FOR CATEGORICAL FEATURES")
print("=" * 50)

from sklearn.preprocessing import OneHotEncoder
from sklearn.compose import ColumnTransformer
import numpy as np

# Identify which categorical features need one-hot encoding
# Typically, we use one-hot encoding for features with low cardinality
print("🔍 Analyzing categorical features for one-hot encoding...")

for feature in categorical_features:
    unique_count = df_processed[feature].nunique()
    print(f"   • {feature}: {unique_count} unique values")

# Let's use one-hot encoding for 'transmission' (usually low cardinality)
# and keep label encoding for 'model' and 'fuelType' (higher cardinality)
one_hot_features = ['transmission']  # Adjust based on your dataset

if one_hot_features:
    print(f"\n🎯 Applying One-Hot Encoding to: {one_hot_features}")
    
    # Find the column indices for one-hot encoding
    one_hot_indices = [X_columns.index(col) for col in one_hot_features if col in X_columns]
    
    print(f"   • One-hot encoding indices: {one_hot_indices}")
    print(f"   • Features to encode: {[X_columns[i] for i in one_hot_indices]}")
    
    # Apply One-Hot Encoding
    ct = ColumnTransformer(
        transformers=[
            ('encoder', OneHotEncoder(drop='first', sparse_output=False), one_hot_indices)
        ], 
        remainder='passthrough'
    )
    
    X_encoded_oh = ct.fit_transform(X_encoded)
    
    # Get feature names after one-hot encoding
    feature_names = []
    for i, transformer in enumerate(ct.transformers_):
        if transformer[0] == 'encoder':
            # Get one-hot encoded feature names
            oh_features = transformer[1].get_feature_names_out(one_hot_features)
            feature_names.extend(oh_features)
        else:
            # Get remaining feature names
            remaining_indices = transformer[2]
            remaining_features = [X_columns[idx] for idx in remaining_indices]
            feature_names.extend(remaining_features)
    
    print(f"✅ One-hot encoding completed!")
    print(f"   • Original shape: {X_encoded.shape}")
    print(f"   • New shape: {X_encoded_oh.shape}")
    print(f"   • New features: {len(feature_names)}")
    
    # Display the transformed features
    print("\n📋 FEATURES AFTER ONE-HOT ENCODING:")
    X_oh_preview = pd.DataFrame(X_encoded_oh, columns=feature_names)
    display(X_oh_preview.head().style.set_caption("Features After One-Hot Encoding") \
           .background_gradient(cmap='viridis'))
    
    # Update X for further processing
    X_processed = X_encoded_oh.copy()
    processed_feature_names = feature_names.copy()
    
else:
    print("ℹ️ No features selected for one-hot encoding")
    X_processed = X_encoded.copy()
    processed_feature_names = X_columns.copy()

})

Model Training and Evaluation Function¶

In [41]:
# Model Training and Evaluation Function (Optimized)
print("\n⚡ TRAINING AND EVALUATING MODELS - OPTIMIZED")
print("=" * 55)

from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestRegressor, ExtraTreesRegressor
from sklearn.metrics import r2_score, mean_absolute_error, mean_squared_error
import time

# Initialize models with optimized parameters for faster training
models = {
    'Linear Regression': LinearRegression(),
    'Random Forest': RandomForestRegressor(random_state=42, n_estimators=50, max_depth=10, n_jobs=-1),
    'Extra Trees': ExtraTreesRegressor(random_state=42, n_estimators=50, max_depth=10, n_jobs=-1)
}

print("✅ Optimized models initialized:")
for name, model in models.items():
    print(f"   • {name}")

def train_and_evaluate_model(model, model_name, X_train, X_test, Y_train, Y_test):
    """
    Train a model and evaluate its performance
    """
    print(f"\n🎯 Training {model_name}...")
    
    # Train model with progress indication
    start_time = time.time()
    model.fit(X_train, Y_train)
    training_time = time.time() - start_time
    
    # Predictions
    Y_pred = model.predict(X_test)
    
    # Calculate metrics
    r2 = r2_score(Y_test, Y_pred)
    mae = mean_absolute_error(Y_test, Y_pred)
    mse = mean_squared_error(Y_test, Y_pred)
    rmse = np.sqrt(mse)
    
    # Display results
    print(f"✅ {model_name} trained in {training_time:.4f} seconds")
    print(f"   📊 R² Score: {r2:.4f}")
    print(f"   💰 MAE: £{mae:,.2f}")
    print(f"   📏 RMSE: £{rmse:,.2f}")
    
    return {
        'Model': model_name,
        'Training Time (s)': training_time,
        'R2 Score': r2,
        'MAE': mae,
        'MSE': mse,
        'RMSE': rmse,
        'Predictions': Y_pred,
        'Model Object': model
    }

⚡ TRAINING AND EVALUATING MODELS - OPTIMIZED
=======================================================
✅ Optimized models initialized:
   • Linear Regression
   • Random Forest
   • Extra Trees

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(18, 5))
fig.suptitle('Residual Analysis - Prediction Errors', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold')

models_for_residuals = [
    ('Linear Regression', model_results['Linear Regression']['Predictions'], 'blue'),
    ('Random Forest', model_results['Random Forest']['Predictions'], 'green'),
    ('Extra Trees', model_results['Extra Trees']['Predictions'], 'orange')
]

for idx, (name, predictions, color) in enumerate(models_for_residuals):
    residuals = Y_test - predictions
    
    # Residual plot
    axes[idx].scatter(predictions, residuals, alpha=0.6, color=color)
    axes[idx].axhline(y=0, color='red', linestyle='--', linewidth=2)
    axes[idx].set_xlabel('Predicted Price (£)')
    axes[idx].set_ylabel('Residuals (£)')
    axes[idx].set_title(f'{name}\nResiduals vs Predicted')
    axes[idx].grid(True, alpha=0.3)
    
    # Add residual statistics
    mean_residual = np.mean(residuals)
    std_residual = np.std(residuals)
    axes[idx].text(0.05, 0.95, f'Mean: £{mean_residual:,.0f}\nStd: £{std_residual:,.0f}', 
                  transform=axes[idx].transAxes, verticalalignment='top',
                  bbox=dict(boxstyle='round', facecolor='white', alpha=0.8))

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

print("✅ Residual analysis completed!")

errors_data = {
    'Linear Regression': Y_test - model_results['Linear Regression']['Predictions'],
    'Random Forest': Y_test - model_results['Random Forest']['Predictions'],

}

for idx, (name, errors) in enumerate(errors_data.items()):
    # Histogram of errors
    axes[idx].hist(errors, bins=30, alpha=0.7, color=['blue', 'green', 'orange'][idx], edgecolor='black')
    axes[idx].axvline(x=0, color='red', linestyle='--', linewidth=2, label='Zero Error')
    axes[idx].axvline(x=np.mean(errors), color='black', linestyle='-', linewidth=2, label=f'Mean: £{np.mean(errors):,.0f}')
    axes[idx].set_xlabel('Prediction Error (£)')
    axes[idx].set_ylabel('Frequency')
    axes[idx].set_title(f'{name}\nError Distribution')
    axes[idx].legend()
    axes[idx].grid(True, alpha=0.3)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# Error statistics table
print("\n📈 ERROR STATISTICS SUMMARY:")
error_stats = []
for name, errors in errors_data.items():
    error_stats.append({
        'Model': name,
        'Mean_Error': np.mean(errors),
        'Std_Error': np.std(errors),
        'MAE': mean_absolute_error(Y_test, Y_test - errors),
        'Max_Overprediction': np.min(errors),  # Most negative error
        'Max_Underprediction': np.max(errors)   # Most positive error
    })

error_stats_df = pd.DataFrame(error_stats)

       .format({

           'Std_Error': '£{:,.2f}',
           'MAE': '£{:,.2f}',
           'Max_Overprediction': '£{:,.2f}',

# Calculate accuracy within different tolerance ranges
print("\n🎯 PREDICTION ACCURACY WITHIN TOLERANCE RANGES:")
tolerance_ranges = [1000, 2500, 5000, 10000]

tolerance_data = []
for name, errors in errors_data.items():
    abs_errors = np.abs(errors)
    tolerance_row = {'Model': name}
    for tolerance in tolerance_ranges:
        within_tolerance = np.sum(abs_errors <= tolerance) / len(abs_errors) * 100
        tolerance_row[f'Within_{tolerance}'] = within_tolerance
    tolerance_data.append(tolerance_row)

tolerance_df = pd.DataFrame(tolerance_data)

# Fixed: Use simple column names for formatting
styled_tolerance = tolerance_df.style.set_caption("Percentage of Predictions Within Tolerance Ranges") \
       .background_gradient(cmap='Greens', vmin=0, vmax=100) \
       .format({
           'Within_1000': '{:.1f}%',
           'Within_2500': '{:.1f}%', 
           'Within_5000': '{:.1f}%',
           'Within_10000': '{:.1f}%'
       })

display(styled_tolerance)

print("\n✅ Error analysis completed successfully!")

ax1.grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='x')

# Add value labels on bars
for i, v in enumerate(top_features['Importance']):
    ax1.text(v + 0.001, i, f'{v:.3f}', va='center', fontweight='bold')

# Plot 2: Pie chart (Top 10 features)
top_10 = importance_df.head(10)
other_importance = importance_df['Importance'][10:].sum()

# Add "Other" category if there are more than 10 features
if len(importance_df) > 10:
    pie_data = pd.concat([top_10, pd.DataFrame({'Feature': ['Other Features'], 
                                              'Importance': [other_importance]})])
else:
    pie_data = top_10

wedges, texts, autotexts = ax2.pie(pie_data['Importance'], 
                                  labels=pie_data['Feature'],
                                  autopct='%1.1f%%',
                                  startangle=90,
                                  colors=plt.cm.Set3(np.linspace(0, 1, len(pie_data))))

# Improve text appearance
for autotext in autotexts:
    autotext.set_color('white')
    autotext.set_fontweight('bold')

ax2.set_title('Feature Importance Distribution\n(Top 10 + Others)', fontweight='bold')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Cumulative Importance Analysis¶

In [65]:
# Cumulative Importance Analysis
print("\n📊 CUMULATIVE FEATURE IMPORTANCE ANALYSIS")
print("=" * 45)

# Calculate cumulative importance
importance_df_sorted = importance_df.sort_values('Importance', ascending=False)
importance_df_sorted['Cumulative_Importance'] = importance_df_sorted['Importance'].cumsum()
importance_df_sorted['Percentage'] = importance_df_sorted['Importance'] * 100
importance_df_sorted['Cumulative_Percentage'] = importance_df_sorted['Cumulative_Importance'] * 100

print("📈 CUMULATIVE IMPORTANCE BREAKDOWN:")
cumulative_display = importance_df_sorted[['Feature', 'Importance', 'Cumulative_Importance', 'Cumulative_Percentage']].head(10)

display(cumulative_display.style.set_caption("Cumulative Feature Importance (Top 10)") \
       .background_gradient(cmap='Blues', subset=['Importance']) \
       .background_gradient(cmap='Greens', subset=['Cumulative_Importance', 'Cumulative_Percentage']) \
       .format({
           'Importance': '{:.4f}',
           'Cumulative_Importance': '{:.4f}',
           'Cumulative_Percentage': '{:.1f}%'
       }))

# Find how many features explain 80%, 90%, 95% of importance
thresholds = [0.80, 0.90, 0.95]
print("\n🎯 FEATURE REDUCTION INSIGHTS:")
for threshold in thresholds:
    num_features = len(importance_df_sorted[importance_df_sorted['Cumulative_Importance'] <= threshold])
    if num_features < len(importance_df_sorted):
        print(f"   • {threshold*100:.0f}% of importance explained by {num_features} features "
              f"(out of {len(importance_df_sorted)})")
    else:
        print(f"   • {threshold*100:.0f}% threshold requires all features")

# Feature Importance Insights and Business Implications
print("\n💡 BUSINESS INSIGHTS FROM FEATURE IMPORTANCE")

# Get top 5 features
top_5_features = importance_df.head(5)

print("🏆 TOP 5 FEATURES DRIVING CAR PRICES:")
for i, (idx, row) in enumerate(top_5_features.iterrows(), 1):
    print(f"   {i}. {row['Feature']} (Importance: {row['Importance']:.3f})")

print("\n📋 BUSINESS RECOMMENDATIONS:")
print("   1. Focus on features with highest importance for pricing strategy")
print("   2. Consider feature engineering for important features")
print("   3. For model simplification, consider removing low-importance features")

# Create a summary table of insights
insights_data = []
for idx, row in top_5_features.iterrows():
    feature = row['Feature']
    importance = row['Importance']
    
    # Generate insights based on feature names
    if 'year' in feature.lower():
        insight = "Newer cars command higher prices - age is a key pricing factor"
    elif 'mileage' in feature.lower():
        insight = "Lower mileage increases car value - maintenance history matters"
    elif 'engine' in feature.lower():
        insight = "Larger engine sizes correlate with higher prices"
    elif 'transmission' in feature.lower():
        insight = "Transmission type significantly affects pricing"
    elif 'model' in feature.lower():
        insight = "Car model series is a major price determinant"
    elif 'fuel' in feature.lower():
        insight = "Fuel type impacts both price and operating costs"
    elif 'tax' in feature.lower():
        insight = "Tax costs influence overall ownership costs"
    elif 'mpg' in feature.lower():
        insight = "Fuel efficiency affects long-term value"
    else:
        insight = "Important pricing factor - consider in valuation"
    
    insights_data.append({
        'Feature': feature,
        'Importance': importance,
        'Business_Insight': insight
    })

insights_df = pd.DataFrame(insights_data)
display(insights_df.style.set_caption("Feature Importance Business Insights") \
       .background_gradient(cmap='YlOrBr', subset=['Importance']) \
       .set_properties(subset=['Business_Insight'], **{'width': '400px'}))

print("\n✅ Feature importance analysis completed!")
print("   Next: Final Project Summary and Export")

# Prediction function
def predict_car_price(model, model_name, year, transmission, mileage, fuel, car_type, tax, mpg, engine_size):
    """
    Predict car price based on input features
    """
    try:
        # Create input array in the same order as training features
        # You'll need to adjust this based on your actual feature order
        input_features = np.array([[
            model, year, transmission, mileage, fuel, car_type, tax, mpg, engine_size
        ]])
        
        # Apply the same preprocessing as training
        # This is a simplified version - you'll need to use your actual preprocessing pipeline
        processed_input = preprocess_input(input_features, label_encoders, scaler, feature_names)
        
        # Make prediction
        prediction = model.predict(processed_input)
        
        return float(prediction[0])
    
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"❌ Prediction error: {e}")
        return None

def preprocess_input(input_data, label_encoders, scaler, feature_names):
    """
    Preprocess input data using the same pipeline as training
    This is a simplified version - you'll need to implement your actual preprocessing
    """
    # For demo purposes, return a random array with correct shape
    # Replace this with your actual preprocessing logic
    return np.random.rand(1, len(feature_names))

# Button click handlers
def on_predict_button_clicked(b):
    with output:
        clear_output()
        
        if loaded_model is None:
            print("❌ Model not loaded properly!")
            return
            
        # Get all input values
        car_model = model_dropdown.value
        car_year = year_slider.value
        car_transmission = transmission_dropdown.value
        car_mileage = mileage_slider.value
        car_fuel = fuel_dropdown.value
        car_type = type_dropdown.value
        car_tax = tax_slider.value
        car_mpg = mpg_slider.value
        car_engine = engine_slider.value
        
        # Display input summary
        print("📋 CAR SPECIFICATIONS:")
        print("=" * 30)
        print(f"   Model: {car_model}")
        print(f"   Year: {car_year}")
        print(f"   Transmission: {car_transmission}")
        print(f"   Mileage: {car_mileage:,} miles")
        print(f"   Fuel Type: {car_fuel}")
        print(f"   Car Type: {car_type}")
        print(f"   Tax: £{car_tax}")
        print(f"   MPG: {car_mpg}")
        print(f"   Engine Size: {car_engine}L")
        print("=" * 30)
        
        # Make prediction
        print("\n🔮 PREDICTING PRICE...")
        predicted_price = predict_car_price(
            loaded_model, model_package['model_name'],
            car_year, car_transmission, car_mileage, 
            car_fuel, car_type, car_tax, car_mpg, car_engine
        )
        
        if predicted_price is not None:
            print(f"\n🎉 PREDICTED CAR PRICE: £{predicted_price:,.2f}")
            
            # Add some context
            if predicted_price > 50000:
                price_category = "💎 Luxury Vehicle"
            elif predicted_price > 30000:
                price_category = "⭐ Premium Vehicle"
            elif predicted_price > 15000:
                price_category = "🚙 Mid-Range Vehicle"
            else:
                price_category = "💰 Budget Vehicle"
                
            print(f"   Category: {price_category}")
            
            # Show confidence based on model performance
            confidence = model_package['model_performance']['r2_score'] * 100
            print(f"   Model Confidence: {confidence:.1f}%")
            
        else:
            print("❌ Could not generate prediction. Please check inputs.")

def on_clear_button_clicked(b):
    # Reset all widgets to default values
    model_dropdown.value = 'A4'
    year_slider.value = 2018
    transmission_dropdown.value = 'Automatic'
    mileage_slider.value = 25000
    fuel_dropdown.value = 'Petrol'
    type_dropdown.value = 'Saloon'
    tax_slider.value = 150
    mpg_slider.value = 45.0
    engine_slider.value = 2.0
    
    with output:
        clear_output()
        print("🔄 All inputs cleared! Ready for new prediction.")

# Attach event handlers
predict_button.on_click(on_predict_button_clicked)
clear_button.on_click(on_clear_button_clicked)
